id: title:Piccirello:allow the stripe and turnstile scripts

review.posthog_relevance: Adds Stripe and Cloudflare Turnstile origins to the CSP script-src directive, potentially preventing CSP violations when HogQL editor or session replay uses these services.
review.reason: Adds two external origins to the CSP script-src directive: Stripe and Cloudflare Turnstile. This could prevent CSP violations when these third-party services are used, potentially improving compatibility or reducing false positives in CSP enforcement.
review.uncertainty: The actual benefit depends on whether Stripe and Cloudflare Turnstile are currently being used and causing violations; this is not demonstrated by the code alone. No tests or error handling are visible in this hunk.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single hunk. No other hunks are supplied, so no relationship between PRs can be established. No score is assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds two external origins to the CSP script-src directive: Stripe and Cloudflare Turnstile. The comment explains that Stripe and Turnstile require loading from their own origins, and these are added to allow their scripts while keeping the policy report-only or restrictive. The comment also notes that frame-src already admits the iframes, and neither produced connect-src violations
observations.posthog_connection: This change relaxes the Content Security Policy for the HogQL editor and session replay components, allowing scripts from Stripe and Cloudflare Turnstile. This could prevent CSP violations when these third-party services are used, potentially improving compatibility or reducing false positives in CSP enforcement.
